name: Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands (cross-save)
post_apply_message:
Ghost Recon Wildlands cross-save — the sync tool is now at ~/wildlands-save-sync/ and the launch guard is set. FOUR MANUAL STEPS REMAIN; the recipe cannot do any of them.

APPLY THIS IN DESKTOP MODE, NOT GAME MODE. The launch-options write needs Steam closed, and in Game Mode gamescope respawns Steam in under a second (measured on the Legion: pid 20535 -> 22956 within 3s). The fresh instance re-reads localconfig.vdf at startup and clobbers the write on its next exit — silently, so it looks like it worked. If you applied this in Game Mode, re-apply from Desktop Mode.

1. RUN THE GAME ONCE through Steam and sign in to Ubisoft Connect. The Proton prefix and the savegames/<GUID>/3559 folder do not exist until you have.

2. RUN SETUP:
     python3 ~/wildlands-save-sync/wl_save_sync.py setup
   Finds or creates the save folder and turns Connect's cloud sync off inside the prefix. Cloud sync MUST stay off — with it on, Connect can pull its stale server-side copy over a good synced save. The guard re-asserts this at every launch.

3. INSTALL SYNCTHING, then add the peers:
     python3 ~/wildlands-save-sync/wl_save_sync.py add-folder --peer "TONY_MAIN_PC,NAS,HTPC"

4. ACCEPT THE NEW DEVICE ON THE OTHER THREE MACHINES — the NAS, the main PC and the HTPC. A reimaged handheld installs a fresh Syncthing with a BRAND-NEW device ID, so none of them will recognise it and every folder share has to be re-established from their side. This has already gone wrong twice: the NAS is carrying two dead handheld device entries from previous reimages, and the live Legion silently inherited none of their folder shares. Prune the stale entries while you are in there.

5. CONFIRM BEFORE PLAYING:
     python3 ~/wildlands-save-sync/wl_save_sync.py status
   Shows peer completion and flags any .sync-conflict-* files. Peer-completion figures are stale for about a minute after a reconnect — if it looks wrong, compare file sizes rather than trusting the percentage.

THE RULE THAT KEEPS THIS WORKING: never play on two machines while one is offline. Run status first if you are unsure.

LOSSLESS SCALING: the launch options above include your ~/lsfg wrapper, because the launch_options step writes the value wholesale — there is no append. If you change how Lossless Scaling is invoked, edit this recipe's value too, or Verify will report NOT_APPLIED.
notes:
Built 2026-08-12 from D:\Linux Prefix Manager\wildlands-save-sync\ (GFM-RECIPE-HANDOFF.md + README.md). The working four-node mesh — main PC, Legion Go 2, HTPC, NAS — predates this recipe; the recipe exists so the LEGION half survives a SteamOS reimage.

SCOPE IS THE LEGION ONLY, per gfm-recipes-target-linux. The Windows machines run the same tool but are set up independently and are not reimaged.

VERIFIED: appid 460930 and install_dir /home/deck/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/Wildlands both confirmed against the live sd_map (buildid 24446260). No other recipe claims 460930.

marker_files GRW.exe is NOT verified on disk — the game sits on the Deck's internal SSD, which isn't reachable from the workstation. It comes from the README's observed process behaviour ('GRW.exe starts, hands off to Ubisoft Connect and dies within ~2 seconds'). Detection resolves by steam_appid first, so the marker is only a fallback; correct it if a scan ever fails to match by name.

PLACEHOLDER TRAP, deliberately different between the two steps: copy_files 'to' goes through Ctx.resolve_target (expands ~, {game_dir}, {prefix}, {localappdata}), but launch_options has its OWN _expand that handles {home} ONLY. Using ~ in the launch options would write a literal ~ into localconfig.vdf. Hence ~ in one step and {home} in the other — not an inconsistency.

PAYLOAD is wl_save_sync.py + README.md. Deliberately NOT wl-guard.bat (Windows-only), wl-save-sync.log, or the handoff doc.

THREE THINGS THIS RECIPE CANNOT DO, all in post_apply_message:
  1. Connect's cloud-sync toggle is nested YAML (user: syncsavegames:) and ini_edit is section/key INI. No step added on purpose — wl_save_sync.py setup already does it, is prefix-aware and fails gracefully with no prefix. A run_command step would cover it but would turn recipes into arbitrary code execution in a public repo; that is Tony's call, not a default.
  2. Syncthing device pairing is inherently multi-machine — the peers must accept the new device ID, which a recipe running on the handheld cannot do.
  3. The prefix does not exist until the game has run once, which is why setup is step 1 of the manual remainder rather than a step here.

DO NOT ADD POST-EXIT MACHINERY TO THE GUARD. It was built and deliberately removed on 2026-08-12: Syncthing's watcher already pushes within ~5s, the guard cannot inhibit suspend so it never covered the case it was for, and it carried a hand-off race that made it a no-op (GRW.exe dies ~2s in, so a post-exit wait saw 'not running' and pushed before the game had written). The README records the evidence. It is pre-launch only, on purpose.

UNTESTED on hardware.
